title: Rapier shapes, meshes & the character controller

recipes.name: Pick parry 0.30.2 shapes by body role: primitives, convex or compound on moving bodies, trimeshes on fixed
recipes.what: At parry3d-f64 0.30.2 SharedShape covers ball, cuboid, capsule, cylinder, cone, round variants, convex polyhedra, compounds, trimeshes, heightfields and voxels; a TriMesh has no interior, so it belongs on fixed bodies only.
recipes.how: Bodies that move: SharedShape::cuboid(hx, hy, hz) / ball / capsule_y(half_height, radius) / cylinder, ColliderBuilder::convex_mesh(points, &indices) for one hull, or ColliderBuilder::compound(vec![(Pose, SharedShape), ..]) of convex parts for a concave object. Fixed level geometry: ColliderBuilder::trimesh_with_flags(vertices, indices, flags) on RigidBodyBuilder::fixed(), and ColliderBuilder::heightfield_with_flags for terrain. Voxels exist at this pin (SharedShape::voxels(voxel_size, &[IVector]), voxels_from_points, voxelized_mesh; ShapeType::Voxels). Rapier's MeshConverter (TriMesh, TriMeshWithFlags, Obb, Aabb, ConvexHull, ConvexDecomposition, ConvexDecompositionWithParams) with ColliderBuilder::converted_trimesh picks a conversion at runtime.
recipes.gotchas: An open trimesh has mass 0 and ccd_thickness 0 (measured), so a dynamic body carrying one gets no mass from it and bodies can pass into its hollow inside. A closed, outward-wound trimesh does report its volume (1/6 for the unit tetrahedron, the same as its convex hull), which makes a trimesh on a dynamic body look fine when it is not. Rapier's guide discourages trimeshes and polylines on dynamic bodies and recommends a convex decomposition in a compound. That guide page is labelled Rust 0.36; every API name above was checked on docs.rs at the pins.
recipes.engine_note: solver/src/rapier_law.rs builds only ColliderBuilder::cuboid colliders (static slabs and every body), one ColliderBuilder::heightfield, and character_shape's SharedShape::cuboid / capsule_y for the controller. The post-Phase-2 collision-from-meshes slice should put TriMesh only on RigidBodyBuilder::fixed() and give dynamic bodies convex_mesh or compound colliders; Signature's geom hash would then have to cover the mesh buffers the way it covers collider rows today.

recipes.name: Validate mesh buffers before TriMesh::with_flags: parry 0.30.2 drops TopologyError and panics on bad indices
recipes.what: TriMesh::new and with_flags return Err only for an empty index buffer (EmptyIndices); a TopologyError under HALF_EDGE_TOPOLOGY is discarded (Ok, topology() == None), NaN and infinite vertices are accepted, and an index past the vertex buffer panics.
recipes.how: Refuse before parry: at least one triangle, every coordinate finite, every index < vertices.len(), no triangle repeating an index. Build with TriMesh::new(vertices, indices), then call mesh.set_flags(TriMeshFlags::HALF_EDGE_TOPOLOGY), which does return Result<(), TopologyError> (BadTriangle(u32) or BadAdjacentTrianglesOrientation { triangle1, triangle2, edge }), and refuse on Err, or check mesh.topology().is_some() after with_flags. Return refusals as an enum, never as a panic.
recipes.gotchas: The docs.rs page says with_flags errors when HALF_EDGE_TOPOLOGY is set and the topology is invalid; the pinned source runs `let _ = result.set_flags(flags);` and the oracle gets Ok with no topology while flags() still claims HALF_EDGE_TOPOLOGY. Two TopologyError doc tests are commented out in the source as failing. A NaN vertex is left out of the local AABB (x = [0, 0] measured for a triangle with a NaN x), so the bounding volume no longer describes the triangle. Index 7 on 3 vertices panics with 'index out of bounds' in rebuild_bvh. Rapier 0.35's quarantine acts on bodies and colliders that go non-finite during a step; it is not a load-time validator.
recipes.engine_note: The post-Phase-2 mesh loader must refuse before any parry call, the way signature() refuses body rows today (bad() on every f64, canon_quat on rotations): solver/Cargo.toml's release profile has panic = "abort", so parry's index panic inside TriMesh::new would trap the wasm module instead of making solver_load return 0.

recipes.name: Canonicalise -0.0 and weld vertices offline: MERGE_DUPLICATE_VERTICES keys raw bits and renumbers the mesh
recipes.what: MERGE_DUPLICATE_VERTICES (and FIX_INTERNAL_EDGES, whose bits 144 include it) keys vertices by raw bytes but compares with ==, so (-0.0, 0, 0) welds to (0, 0, 0) in a 4- or 16-vertex mesh and not in a 64-vertex one; merging also renumbers and drops unreferenced vertices, and DELETE_DEGENERATE_TRIANGLES only removes repeated-index triangles.
recipes.how: In the offline tool: pass every coordinate through canon() (x == 0.0 -> 0.0), refuse NaN, weld exact duplicates yourself, drop zero-area triangles by computing their area, and write the vertex buffer in first-reference order with every vertex referenced. Such buffers pass through FIX_INTERNAL_EDGES unchanged (measured), so the stored bytes are the bytes parry uses. Never keep outside references to input vertex indices across a merging flag.
recipes.gotchas: TriMeshFlags documents MERGE as joining 'vertices with the exact same coordinates' and TriMesh documents vertices() as keeping construction order; signed zero breaks the first, and any merging flag breaks the second (7 vertices in, 4 out, (9, 9, 9) dropped). The ±0 result depends on hash-table probing: the key hashes the raw bytes, equality is ==, and under enhanced-determinism the map is an IndexMap with FxHasher32. Whether the flip point differs on wasm32 was not measured. A mesh whose every triangle repeats an index comes back with 0 triangles, not EmptyIndices, because the emptiness check runs before the deletion. A zero-area triangle with three distinct indices is kept.
recipes.engine_note: signature() in rapier_law.rs mixes every geometry f64 with mix_f64 (to_bits), so -0.0 and 0.0 already give different world signatures. The mesh slice's offline tool should apply the same canon() that write_body uses, and the loader should refuse a non-canonical value, which is the pattern T3's load-time refusal of non-finite authored values already follows.

recipes.name: Compute convex hulls and VHACD parts offline with pinned parameters, then load stored buffers with convex_mesh
recipes.what: SharedShape::convex_hull is None for fewer than 3 points, NaN, coincident or collinear points, but Some for coplanar points: a flat polyhedron of mass 0. VHACD output follows its parameters: a two-box mesh of volume 2 became 2 parts (mass 2.0000) at resolution 64 and 13 parts (summed mass 3.1227) at resolution 16.
recipes.how: Offline: parry3d_f64::transformation::try_convex_hull(&points) -> (vertices, indices); refuse Err and refuse a hull whose mass_properties(1.0).mass() is 0. For concave parts call SharedShape::convex_decomposition_with_params(&v, &idx, &VHACDParameters { .. }) with every field written out (0.30.2 defaults: resolution 64, concavity 0.01, alpha 0.05, beta 0.05, plane_downsampling 4, convex_hull_downsampling 4, convex_hull_approximation true, max_convex_hulls 1024) and store each part's vertex and index buffers. At load: ColliderBuilder::convex_mesh(points, &indices) per part, which skips the hull computation and gave the same mass bits as convex_hull, then ColliderBuilder::compound.
recipes.gotchas: ConvexHullError's docs say nearly coplanar 3D input gives MissingSupportPoint; the pinned code triangulates coplanar input as a flat hull and from_convex_mesh accepts it (measured Some, mass 0), and ColliderBuilder::convex_hull ('None if the points don't form a valid convex shape') and MeshConverter::ConvexHull pass it too (both returned a mass-0 shape). The hull code counts dimensions with a 1.0e-7 eigenvalue threshold, so a nearly flat cloud can land on either side. VHACD memory grows as O(resolution^3) and convex_hull_approximation = false costs 2-5x time (VHACDParameters docs). A summed compound mass above the source volume means overlapping parts.
recipes.engine_note: The post-Phase-2 slice plans 'hull point sets stored offline for determinism': store try_convex_hull's vertex and triangle-index buffers rather than only the points, load them with ColliderBuilder::convex_mesh, and refuse a mass-0 hull at load. VHACD belongs in the offline tool: its O(resolution^3) voxel grid would be a transient allocation inside a solver binary whose memory T3's lint forbids from growing.

recipes.name: Fill a parry HeightField column-major with scale as the whole extent, and sample it as two triangles per cell
recipes.what: In HeightField::new(Array2::new(nrows, ncols, data), scale) row i advances z and column j advances x, data is column-major (i + j * nrows), scale is the whole field (cell width = scale.x / (ncols - 1)), the field is centred on its collider, and each cell is two triangles split along (x0, z1)-(x1, z0), not a bilinear patch.
recipes.how: Build with Array2::from_fn(rows, cols, |row, col| h[row][col]), or transpose a row-major record with data[row + col * rows] = record[row * cols + col]; pass scale = ((cols - 1) * cell, 1.0, (rows - 1) * cell). Code that samples the surface outside the solver must use the same triangles: in cell (i, j) with fractions u (x) and v (z), h = h00 + u*(h01 - h00) + v*(h10 - h00) when u + v <= 1, else h = h11 + (1-u)*(h10 - h11) + (1-v)*(h01 - h11), where h10 is the +z neighbour and h01 the +x neighbour, or it can ask the law with a downward ray.
recipes.gotchas: Rapier's ColliderBuilder::heightfield doc at 0.35.3 calls scale the 'Size of each grid cell'; parry divides it by (ncols - 1), so a scale of (1, 1, 1) on 5 columns gives cells 0.25 wide (measured). HeightField::new asserts at least 2 rows and columns and Array2::new asserts data.len() == nrows * ncols; both are panics. Bilinear interpolation disagrees with the solver on any non-planar cell: 0.25 against 0 at the centre of a unit cell with one corner raised by 1 (measured). A cell flagged HeightFieldCellStatus::ZIGZAG_SUBDIVISION uses the other diagonal.
recipes.engine_note: build_world in rapier_law.rs transposes the row-major HEIGHTS buffer with data[row + col * rows] and passes ((cols - 1) * cell, 1, (rows - 1) * cell) on a fixed body at the origin, which matches parry, and signature() refuses fewer than 2 rows or columns before HeightField's assert can fire; MAX_HEIGHTS 256 caps a field at 256 heights (16 x 16, say). packages/tick/world.js heightfieldSupport, which supportAt hands to the verb predicates, interpolates bilinearly, so on a non-planar cell it reports a height the solver's surface does not have.

recipes.name: Set FIX_INTERNAL_EDGES on ground dynamic bodies slide over; test heightfield row 0 moving +x on its own
recipes.what: Without the flag, a frictionless box sliding flat at 2 u/s stopped dead at the first internal edge of a trimesh or heightfield (0.25 of 2.00 travelled in 64 quanta) because the edge adds a sideways contact normal. TriMeshFlags::FIX_INTERNAL_EDGES removed the snag; on a 9 x 9 heightfield, HeightFieldFlags::FIX_INTERNAL_EDGES removed it for every row and column in both directions except moving +x in row 0, the lowest-z row of cells.
recipes.how: ColliderBuilder::trimesh_with_flags(v, idx, TriMeshFlags::FIX_INTERNAL_EDGES) and ColliderBuilder::heightfield_with_flags(heights, scale, HeightFieldFlags::FIX_INTERNAL_EDGES) for any ground a dynamic body slides or rolls on; triangle_normal_constraints(id).is_some() confirms the pseudo-normals exist. Keep an outcome test per direction that crosses a seam in row 0 and in an interior row. Padding a field with one extra row on its low-z side, so nothing moves in row 0, is a workaround inferred from the measurement, not from any source.
recipes.gotchas: The snag is a solver-contact effect: with max_ccd_substeps = 0 it was unchanged, and the kinematic controller walked the same seams with or without the flag (1.985 on a 2-row field, 2.000 on 3 rows, never airborne). A 2-row heightfield is all row 0. TriMeshFlags::FIX_INTERNAL_EDGES also merges duplicate vertices (see the weld recipe). parry's heightfield triangle_normal_constraints says its edge pseudo-normals are 'given in no particular order'; whether that explains the row-0 case is a guess.
recipes.engine_note: build_world calls ColliderBuilder::heightfield with no flags, so T4 pin 3's seam test (a box sliding down across a cell boundary with no upward hitch beyond the skin) is where heightfield_with_flags(.., HeightFieldFlags::FIX_INTERNAL_EDGES) gets measured; adopting it changes the binary digest and the goldens once. That test needs a crossing in row 0 moving +x: a 2-row field, which signature() allows and packages/tick/verbs.test.js uses for its sloped case, has no other row.

recipes.name: Call KinematicCharacterController::move_shape with Absolute lengths and self-exclusion, then apply the result
recipes.what: move_shape sweeps the shape (at most 20 casts, each stopping offset short of obstacles), tries a stair step on every wall hit and otherwise slides, snaps down only if the call started grounded, and returns EffectiveCharacterMovement { translation, grounded, is_sliding_down_slope }; it moves nothing, the caller applies translation.
recipes.how: Set every CharacterLength as Absolute: offset, CharacterAutostep { max_height, min_width, include_dynamic_bodies }, snap_to_ground; write up, slide, max_slope_climb_angle, min_slope_slide_angle (radians) and normal_nudge_factor explicitly. Per quantum: let pos = *world.bodies[h].position(); let q = world.query_pipeline_with_filter(QueryFilter::new().exclude_rigid_body(h)); let mv = ctl.move_shape(dt, &q, &*shape, &pos, desired, |c| collisions.push(c)); world.bodies[h].set_next_kinematic_translation(pos.translation + mv.translation); then step. Pass the shape the body's collider uses, zero vertical velocity on mv.grounded, and read is_sliding_down_slope as advisory.
recipes.gotchas: Defaults are Relative (offset 0.01, snap 0.2, autostep 0.25 and 0.5) and evaluate against the shape's AABB, the height and for min_width the horizontal diagonal: the resting gap was 0.0201 for a 2.0-high box under the default and 0.0101 with Absolute(0.01). Without the self-exclusion filter the walker never moved (0.000 against 0.956). Depenetration runs only when the desired translation is (near) zero, so a walker with any intent is never pushed out that way. is_sliding_down_slope was true on flat ground whenever the move had a downward part. An airborne character stepped up a 0.2 rise (dy 0.2101); the 0.36 guide says autostep needs floor contact first, which the pinned code does not check. The stair probe adds offset to max_height and min_width; the comparisons at the limits are binary-and-limits' finding. parry 0.30.2's shape-cast fix (#429) moved the controller's progress bound in Rapier's own test from 940 to 930.
recipes.engine_note: rapier_law.rs controller() already sets SKIN 0.01, STEP_HEIGHT 0.3, STEP_MIN_WIDTH 0.2 and SNAP 0.2 as CharacterLength::Absolute with CLIMB_ANGLE pi/4, SLIDE_ANGLE 50 degrees in radians and normal_nudge_factor 1e-4, so character_shape can switch between SharedShape::cuboid and capsule_y without moving those lengths; integrate() excludes the walker's own body, applies the move with set_next_kinematic_translation, zeroes vy on grounded and ignores is_sliding_down_slope. fixtures/shape-traversal.json kept the box (docs/PHASE-1.md: it climbs a step of the maximum height and holds a ledge where the same-size capsule misses the step and drops); below the limit both shapes climbed alike here, feet at step + 0.010. Lifted actions (DRIVEN 2.0) bypass move_shape.

recipes.name: Push dynamic bodies with solve_character_collision_impulses and plan all walkers against the last step's poses
recipes.what: move_shape stops a walker one offset short of a dynamic body and never moves it; solve_character_collision_impulses applies approximate impulses to dynamic bodies only. Walkers meet each other as kinematic obstacles at the last step's poses and inherit a touching kinematic body's velocity, so two walkers planned together stayed apart at 1 and 2 u/s but overlapped at 8 u/s.
recipes.how: Collect CharacterCollision events in move_shape's callback, call set_next_kinematic_translation, then build a QueryPipelineMut with broad_phase.as_query_pipeline_mut(narrow_phase.query_dispatcher(), bodies, colliders, filter) excluding the walker and call solve_character_collision_impulses(dt, &mut q, shape, character_mass, &collisions) before world.step(). Run every walker's move_shape before applying any of them; planning order then cannot change the result (reversed order was bit-identical). State the speed in any walker-against-walker outcome test.
recipes.gotchas: Each contact point gets an impulse along the normal only, scaled by body_mass*character_mass/(body_mass + character_mass); the docs call it 'only approximate'. include_dynamic_bodies: false makes the stair probe skip dynamic bodies. Mirror-image walkers did not end mirror-image (-0.2741 and +0.2905 at 1 u/s), so assert separation and 'neither passes the other's start', not symmetry. A kinematic body walking into a standing walker pushed it through the platform path when the walker had any intent (x -0.797, clear) and through depenetration when its intent was zero (x -0.744, 0.006 inside at the end).
recipes.engine_note: integrate() in rapier_law.rs plans every walker with move_shape before any set_next_kinematic_translation, then calls solve_character_collision_impulses with character_mass 1.0 (walkers get additional_mass(1.0)) and include_dynamic_bodies: false. For T4 pin 5's two walkers driven at each other: at the verb speed of 1 u/s (predicates/intents/*.json) they ended 0.0646 apart here; at 8 u/s, above world.js's MAX_SPEED 2, they ended 0.0318 overlapped.

recipes.name: Test line of sight with an eye-to-target ray at max_toi 1.0 on fixed colliders once the broad phase holds them
recipes.what: QueryPipeline::cast_ray(&Ray, max_toi, solid) returns the first (ColliderHandle, toi) with hit point origin + dir * toi, so dir = target - eye with max_toi 1.0 is exactly the eye-to-target segment. Queries see only colliders already in the broad phase, intersect_ray yields hits in tree order, and solid = true answers toi 0 from inside a shape.
recipes.how: let seg = Ray::new(eye, target - eye); let blocked = world.cast_ray(&seg, 1.0, true, QueryFilter::only_fixed()).is_some(); only_fixed() keeps fixed colliders (and parentless ones) and drops every body, the looker and the target included. With a wider filter, exclude the looker (exclude_rigid_body) and the target (a predicate). Use cast_ray_and_get_normal when the normal matters. When several hits are needed, collect intersect_ray or intersect_shape and sort by (toi, collider handle) before anything order-sensitive.
recipes.gotchas: A unit dir makes toi a distance (0.9 here) and target - eye makes it a fraction (0.225); one max_toi cannot serve both. With no filter the looker's own collider answered first at toi 0. Before the first step cast_ray returned None with the walls inserted; the scene-queries guide says stepping updates the broad phase the queries rely on. intersect_ray returned 0.725, 0.475, 0.225, insertion order rather than distance. From inside a wall, solid = false reported the exit at 0.1.
recipes.engine_note: E5 sight runs in the JS tick (distance at most `sight` and a zero-extent swept segment crossing no static collider), and docs/dispatch-e5-minds.md keeps the binary unchanged for it. Once collision-from-meshes adds TriMesh statics, a box-only JS segment test cannot answer; the matching law query is cast_ray(Ray::new(eye, target - eye), 1.0, true) with QueryFilter::only_fixed(), exported like solver_step and run only after solver_load, whose warm_broadphase CollisionPipeline pass is what puts the colliders in the broad phase.

recipes.name: Bake glTF collision meshes offline with the gltf crate and refuse what the deterministic law cannot reproduce
recipes.what: The glTF 2.0 spec fixes meters, radians, +Y up, float32 POSITION with min/max, unit quaternions and in-range indices, but files can still break it; the gltf crate (1.4.1) exposes f32 transforms, Mode, positions, indices and skins. Converting belongs in a host tool that writes baked f64 triangles, not in the wasm law.
recipes.how: Tool: gltf::import the file, walk the scene's nodes and compose each Transform in f64 (matrix() or decomposed()). Refuse a primitive unless mode() == Mode::Triangles, every position is finite, and every index (reader indices, ReadIndices::into_u32) is below the position count and not 255/65535/4294967295 for its width; refuse skins (node.skin()), animations and morph weights on collision nodes. Refuse a rotation with |q.q - 1| above a stated tolerance (1e-6 suits f32 input), refuse zero or non-finite scale, and when the scale's determinant is negative swap two indices per triangle. Write units ('m') and up axis ('+Y') into the record and refuse records without them, then canonicalise -0.0, weld, and store f64 vertex and u32 index buffers (and offline hulls).
recipes.gotchas: gltf's Transform holds f32 arrays: widening to f64 is exact, but composing in f32 is not, so compose in f64 once and store the result so the law never multiplies transforms. f32 sqrt(1/2) quaternions miss unit length by 3.4e-8 (measured), so an exact == 1.0 test refuses valid files. A mirrored node, scale (-1, 1, 1), flips a floor triangle's normal from +Y to -Y and swapping two indices restores it (measured). The spec says a skinned mesh's node transform MUST be ignored, so skinned geometry has no single static shape, and degenerate triangles are only SHOULD NOT. The gltf crate is outside this KB's oracle set: its API was checked on docs.rs, not compiled.
recipes.engine_note: The collision-from-meshes slice after Phase 2 (its input is the studio's glb survey) should keep the gltf crate in host tooling: the law is a wasm32-unknown-unknown cdylib with raw extern "C" exports over static f64 buffers and a pinned digest, and at load it already refuses NaN and renormalises quaternions with canon_quat. The world file carries the baked buffers; solver_load validates them like body rows and mixes them into Signature.geom.

sources.title: Khronos glTF 2.0 Specification (AsciiDoc source)
sources.claim: Linear distances are meters and angles radians, +Y is up; index values MUST be below the attribute count and MUST NOT be 255/65535/4294967295; POSITION is float32 VEC3 with min and max; degenerate triangles SHOULD NOT appear; a skinned mesh's node transform MUST be ignored; a matrix MUST be decomposable to TRS.
